scope: Complete version-controlled source inventory, deterministic local-fixture verification, reset behavior, dashboard/API boundary checks, idempotency behavior, deployment configuration review, and truthful-claim review.
executionBoundary: All verified workflows use local in-memory fixtures. The audit did not connect to AWS, query CloudWatch or Cost Explorer, deploy a Lambda, execute Kiro Crew/CLI/Web, run a Kiro hook or power, or terminate an AWS resource.
sourceRevisionIdentity: The normalized SHA-256 inventory below identifies the complete audited working tree independently of a Git commit. It includes every version-controlled/non-ignored project file except this audit artifact itself. The three visible digest-reference lines are normalized to a fixed token before hashing to avoid an unavoidable artifact-hash self-reference; npm run audit:verify checks both the inventory and the displayed artifact digest.

digestReferenceNormalization.rule: Only the one visible Complete audit artifact SHA-256 line in each listed path is normalized before its file hash is calculated.

automatedTestResult.note: Node TAP counts the outer suite in addition to the named nested checks. The standalone gate runs after the TAP suite.

resetAndIdempotencySmoke.boundary: The engine smoke covers local transitions. Browser-facing API tests additionally verify a validated HttpOnly local-fixture session cookie, so Vercel warm-memory state is not the source of browser demo state. This remains simulated local data, not cloud persistence.

deploymentConfigurationReview.apiEntrypoint: api/index.js is included in the complete inventory and passed syntax validation.
deploymentConfigurationReview.vercelConfiguration: vercel.json is included in the complete inventory and passed JSON parsing. It retains framework: null, api/index.js includeFiles, and catch-all rewrite configuration.
deploymentConfigurationReview.resetRoute: Tests exercise POST /api/reset, wrong method, wrong content type, reset state restoration, a restored subsequent workflow, and per-browser validated session-cookie continuity across fresh engine instances.

staticBoundaryScan.note: These static checks support the stated local-fixture boundary; they are not a substitute for an external security review.

claimReview.dashboard: The dashboard fetches same-origin API state and returned workflow/reset data; it does not use timer-only success. Reset Local Fixture Scenario restores only local in-memory fixtures.
claimReview.reset: POST /api/reset takes an empty JSON object, accepts no external resource/account input, restores only the browser local-fixture session, and reports that no AWS resource was changed.
claimReview.financialInvariant: The legacy fee expression and independent modern BigInt rational oracle agree across deterministic local property trials. Generated modern fixture code is executed in test against the oracle.
claimReview.kiroAssets: Root .kiro assets exist and label themselves illustrative/unverified. Their presence is not runtime execution evidence.
claimReview.receipt: Receipt digest is a SHA-256 integrity check over canonical local-fixture receipt data; it is unsigned and is not proof of a cloud action.
claimReview.license: Root LICENSE is MIT and the public repository identifies its MIT license.

publicationNote: This audit does not establish Devpost completion, public demo-video publication, entrant eligibility, original-project timing, bonus eligibility, actual Kiro runtime use, or actual cloud actions. It records only the listed local-source evidence.
verification: Run npm run audit:verify and sha256sum docs/audit/necroops-fixture-mode-audit-log.json from the exact source revision.
